The best UK universities for History to consider for 2027 entry include Oxford, Cambridge, St Andrews, LSE, Durham, UCL, Warwick, York, Bristol and Exeter. They offer different reasons to apply: intensive tutorials, international history, medieval research, broad module choice or opportunities to combine History with Politics.

There is no single winner for every student. Someone fascinated by diplomacy may prefer a different course from someone who wants to work with medieval manuscripts, even when both could meet the same entry requirements.

This guide compares undergraduate degrees for autumn 2027 entry. It separates published fees from figures awaiting confirmation and uses rankings alongside course content, teaching and affordability. Start with the comparison, then look closely at the programmes that match what you actually want to study.

These are standard offers, not guaranteed admission thresholds. Contextual offers, accepted qualifications and additional subject conditions vary. The official course links in the profiles below provide the relevant detail. Placement and study-abroad routes can extend the standard duration.

How to Read UK History University Rankings

History rankings help you find departments worth investigating. They cannot tell you whether you will enjoy the compulsory modules.

The Complete University Guide's History comparison provides a domestic subject table. Use the edition shown on the page and distinguish a university's History position from its overall institutional ranking.

The Guardian takes a different approach. Its explanation of the 2027 measures covers teaching and assessment satisfaction, resources, continuation, value added and career prospects. St Andrews confirms that it ranks first for History in the Guardian's 2027 guide.

For international context, consult the QS History subject comparison for 2026. Its edition differs from the 2027 UK guides; an application year does not automatically become a ranking year.

A useful surprise: the highest-ranked department may still be the wrong choice for your particular historical interests. Treat a ranking as the beginning of your research, then test the course against your priorities.

A Closer Look at the Best History Degrees in the UK

University of Bristol

Bristol's three-year BA History covers medieval, early modern, modern and contemporary history, with social, cultural, political, environmental and global approaches. Its course outline and recent unit examples include slavery, protest, revolutions and the history of polar regions.

That range suits someone who wants to connect historical arguments with questions about power, identity and the environment. Recent units illustrate the department's interests; they do not guarantee a particular option throughout your degree.

The standard offer is AAA, with ABB for eligible contextual applicants. Bristol currently displays £28,200 for international tuition but explicitly labels it a 2026-entry figure. It has not confirmed the 2027 fee on this page, so avoid treating that amount as your final budget.

University of Cambridge

Cambridge's BA (Hons) History offers broad historical study and opportunities to explore different approaches to interpreting the past. Its course structure and admissions guidance explain the papers, historical thinking and college-specific requirements.

Consider Cambridge if you enjoy moving beyond what happened to ask how historians construct explanations. Close discussion rewards students who prepare carefully, weigh competing arguments and change their position when the evidence demands it.

The published minimum A-level offer is A*AA for 2027 entry; individual colleges can set additional conditions. International tuition is £30,798 for 2027 entry, and most international students also pay a separate college fee. Compare the full cost before assuming Cambridge and another three-year course carry similar price tags.

Durham University

Durham's BA History aims to develop an understanding of human experience across different periods and regions. The published programme and entry requirements set out a standard offer of A*AA, including an A in History.

Durham describes expertise in medieval, early modern and modern history, including Britain, Europe, North America, Africa, and East and South Asia. Its approaches include gender, material culture, science and medicine, and economic and social history. That range offers several starting points for a specialist research interest.

Match those interests to the modules available for your year, then compare assessment and costs. Confirm the current overseas fee directly; this guide does not quote an unverified 2027 amount.

University of Exeter

Exeter's History degree at the Streatham campus offers a three-year route, alongside four-year options with study abroad or employment experience. Its official page confirms tenth place in the Complete University Guide's 2027 History table.

The course encourages comparisons across periods and societies, supported by lectures, seminars, presentations and independent study. This makes it worth considering if you want a broad degree and time to develop a specialism.

The standard offer is AAB. Exeter publishes international tuition of £25,700 a year for 2027 entry. Applicants considering the employment route should know that they take responsibility for finding a placement, with university guidance and approval. Choosing that route does not mean an employer has already reserved a role for you.

London School of Economics and Political Science

LSE's BA History focuses on international history and the forces that shaped the modern world. Its programme content and fee details cover themes such as empire, conflict and relations between societies, with a final-year dissertation.

For a student interested in the Cold War, diplomacy or global political change, that focus may matter more than a university offering a longer chronological range. Someone committed to ancient history should compare other programmes carefully.

LSE asks for AAA and does not make A-level History compulsory. Its 2027/28 overseas fee is £30,400 per year, fixed for the subsequent years of the full-time programme under the published policy. That makes the tuition calculation clearer, although accommodation and everyday spending remain separate.

University of Oxford

Oxford's BA History centres on extensive reading, essay writing and tutorial discussion. Its course and application requirements specify AAA and recommend History at A-level or equivalent.

The appeal is the discussion itself: you prepare an argument, explain your evidence and respond to questions. Students who enjoy that exchange may find the teaching particularly rewarding.

For 2027 entry, Oxford requires written work but no written admissions test for this single-subject course. The written-work deadline is 10 November 2026. Overseas tuition is £46,210 annually, with potential increases in later years. Check joint-degree requirements separately, because Oxford does not apply the same test rules to every course containing History.

University of St Andrews

St Andrews offers a four-year MA (Hons) History. Despite the title, this is an undergraduate degree, not a postgraduate master's qualification.

The programme's early subject choices and honours structure allow students to explore different historical periods and study other subjects before specialising. The curriculum spans ancient, medieval, modern, Scottish and Middle Eastern history.

The standard A-level requirement is AAA, including A in History. Published overseas tuition for September 2027 entry is £34,910 per year.

St Andrews deserves attention if you value exploration before making narrower academic choices. Its extra year creates that space, but also adds another year of living costs. Compare whole-degree spending rather than annual tuition alone.

University College London

UCL's BA History spans regions and periods from the Ancient Near East to modern China, the United States and the Caribbean. Its curriculum, collections and entry criteria make it a useful option for applicants who want to move between ancient, medieval and modern topics.

London's museums and UCL's own collections add opportunities to think about physical objects, archives and public interpretations of the past. Ask how your preferred modules use those resources rather than assuming every class includes collection visits.

UCL requires AAA, including History. International tuition is £33,300 for 2027/28 entrants. The university describes a cohort fee guarantee, subject to its stated exceptions, so read that policy alongside your offer.

University of Warwick

Warwick's BA History offers a global curriculum and room to develop an individual set of historical interests. Its degree pathways and optional intercalated year include the possibility of applying for a year abroad or work placement.

Students can also explore the Renaissance and Modern History route, which includes a term in Venice. That is a specific reason to investigate Warwick if the period interests you, rather than choosing it simply because it appears on a general shortlist.

The typical offer is AAA, including History. Warwick has not yet set its overseas tuition fees for 2027/28. Keep the fee pending in your comparison and confirm it before committing to a financial plan.

University of York

York's BA (Hons) History places small-group teaching at the centre of the degree. Its teaching approach and qualification requirements specify AAA, including A in History or Classical Civilisation.

York also offers an environment worth investigating for archival research, including the university's Borthwick Institute for Archives. If primary sources excite you, ask how undergraduates access collections and develop the skills to interpret them.

For example, an interest in church records becomes a stronger reason to apply when you can identify relevant teaching and a feasible research question. The existence of an archive alone does not guarantee supervision for any topic. Confirm York's current 2027 fee directly before comparing its affordability with the priced options below.

Look for practice in using primary sources and evaluating historians' interpretations, often called historiography. For example, a newspaper report and a private diary may describe the same protest differently. A useful question is how the course teaches you to explain that difference and build a defensible argument.

Here's the thing: a compelling final-year option should not outweigh two years of compulsory modules you dislike. Open the first-year syllabus before browsing dissertation titles.

One practical detail is easy to miss on an open day: the timetable between classes. Reading, travel, paid work and essay deadlines all need to fit into an ordinary week. Picture that week before deciding whether the teaching style suits you.

A general History degree, Ancient History and History of Art are not interchangeable choices. Compare the periods, source material and methods in each syllabus. Likewise, postgraduate History courses answer a different admissions question from the undergraduate programmes here.

Which Universities Offer History and Politics?

If political institutions, ideas and power interest you as much as historical interpretation, compare joint degrees separately.

Oxford's combined study of history and political analysis includes political theory and quantitative methods. Its standard offer is AAA. Crucially, 2027 applicants must take TARA, unlike applicants to Oxford's single-subject History BA. The published test-booking deadline is 28 September 2026 at 18:00 UK time, with tests taking place from 12 to 16 October.

Cambridge combines historical study with politics and international relations in its own joint degree. Warwick's joint honours course provides another option, with a typical AAA offer including History.

Do not assume the highest History ranking identifies the best joint course. Compare the balance between departments, compulsory political theory, research methods and dissertation choices. You may love political history while preferring to spend your entire degree in a History department.

Entry Requirements and 2027 Application Deadlines

The standard offers in this comparison range from AAB to A*AA. Grades form only part of the application: subject preparation, written work and the university's selection process also matter.

The official UCAS application timetable gives these dates:

Schools may set earlier internal deadlines. Arrange references and any required assessments before the university deadline approaches.

When preparing your application, work through your UCAS application and explain what historical reading has taught you. Comparing two interpretations of a revolution says more about your academic interest than listing ten books without discussing them.

International qualifications do not convert into A-level grades through one universal formula. Check each university's country requirements and the English-language evidence universities accept before booking a test. Plan for the named course's autumn start rather than assuming January or May entry exists.

Compare the Whole Cost

LSE and Oxford publish a first-year tuition difference of £15,810. That is a useful comparison, but multiplying it by three would ignore their different fee policies.

For living costs, Oxford estimates £1,475 to £2,175 per month for 2027/28. Nine months therefore means approximately £13,275 to £19,575, before tuition. This is an Oxford estimate, not a universal UK allowance. Check accommodation contract lengths, travel and holiday spending for each location.

Build a Shortlist You Could Actually Accept

Begin with two academic priorities, such as medieval Europe and small-group discussion. Then set a realistic annual and whole-degree budget.

Keep only courses whose compulsory content, requirements and likely costs work for you. Next, plan a balanced set of UCAS choices across realistic admission prospects rather than selecting institutions solely by reputation.

Ask departments focused questions: Does the module run annually? Can undergraduates use the relevant archive? What happens if an optional pathway fills up? Those answers reveal more than another broad claim about academic excellence.

Applicants moving from abroad should also plan the practical steps of studying in Britain, including housing and arrival arrangements. A strong shortlist combines academic interest with an offer you could afford to accept.

What Can You Do with a History Degree?

History develops research, source evaluation and clear written argument. University course pages describe graduate routes into areas such as education, publishing, journalism, public service, heritage and business.

The degree does not guarantee entry into any of them. Use your time at university to test an interest through projects, volunteering or relevant work experience. For instance, helping an organisation turn archival material into an accessible exhibition can show both research and communication skills.

When comparing employment figures, look at the cohort, measurement date and definition of the outcome. A university-wide salary headline cannot predict what a particular History graduate will earn.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which is the best university for History in the UK?

St Andrews ranks first for History in the Guardian University Guide 2027. That gives it a strong claim within that particular ranking, but the best course for you also depends on historical interests, teaching, entry requirements and cost.

Is Oxford or Cambridge better for History?

Compare their course structures and teaching arrangements rather than assuming one wins for everyone. Both require substantial academic preparation. Look particularly at the papers you would take, college conditions and the opportunities to develop your preferred historical interests.

Do I need A-level History to study a History degree?

Not everywhere. LSE does not require it, while UCL and Warwick do. York accepts History or Classical Civilisation within its stated offer. Check the specific programme because universities can set different conditions for joint degrees.

What are the best Russell Group universities for History?

Oxford, Cambridge, Durham, LSE, UCL, Warwick, York, Bristol and Exeter are options in this comparison. Membership alone does not establish which teaches your preferred subject best. St Andrews sits outside the group and remains a strong History choice.

Are the best universities in England for History the same as the UK list?

The lists overlap, but England and the UK are not interchangeable. St Andrews is in Scotland. Students restricting their search to England should compare the other nine institutions here and investigate further courses that meet their needs.

Is a four-year History degree better than a three-year course?

Not automatically. Four years can create room for broader study or an additional experience, but course design matters more than duration alone. Compare the academic benefit with the extra tuition, accommodation and time involved.

Turn Your Comparison into a Decision

The best UK universities for History offer different routes into the subject. Start with the course. Compare the historical periods you want to explore, the way tutors teach and assess your work, and the full cost of completing the degree.

Choose three programmes you can justify in specific terms, then check their subject requirements and application deadlines. A shortlist becomes useful when every option gives you a clear reason to apply. If you need help matching those choices to your qualifications and budget, discuss your university options with an adviser before preparing your application.
